archive: archive/ holds past editions: read only, never run; to rerun one, use the old release install.
step: a release proof, not a loop step: the RUN proof of CLEAN_RELEASE_V1 section 1 (a real run imports and opens code only from the release)
question: Did this run of a release script import code only from the Alarm folder and open, under the forbidden folder, only data under the settings keys?

commands.name: run
commands.does: runs one script of this Alarm folder as __main__ with its arguments, then prints RUN ISOLATION OK or FAILED

args.name: --settings
args.meaning: this machine's settings file (KEY=VALUE lines read by _tools/settings_v1.py); always named on the command line

args.name: --forbid
args.meaning: a folder no code may come from (repeatable); default: the settings' FORBID (folders split on :)

args.name: script.py
args.meaning: a script inside this Alarm folder

commands.writes: nothing itself; the script writes what it writes

refuses.when: refused: no settings file or a bad one, no forbidden folder (neither --forbid nor FORBID), a script outside this Alarm folder; no script (prints the usage)
RUN ISOLATION FAILED: a module from outside, a file under the forbidden folder that is no data of the settings (or is code), or a past edition (archive/) opened or imported

rules: otherwise the exit code is the script's own
the interpreter's own files do not count

outputs.where: stdout, last line, when the run is isolated
stdout, last line, when it is not

dry_run_data: planted by _tools/tests/test_agent_docs_v1.py in a new temp folder: {SETTINGS} its settings file, {WORLD} the folder, {ALARM} this Alarm folder; run AD1_20261029, idea FLOWX
